$janet.$comment: Not JSON Schema. Read by scripts/Test-OutputContracts.ps1, which is the point of the file living here rather than being generated from the return type.
$janet.produces: azure_role_list, azure_role_assign, azure_role_remove (MCP only; no CLI verb)
$janet.$comment.contractField: The envelope stamps 'contract' and the gate cross-checks it against the number above, so code and schema cannot drift apart in either direction.
$janet.$comment.oneEnvelope: One envelope for list, assign and remove, so a caller reads all three the same way. 'operation' says which produced it.
$janet.$comment.everyKey: Every key is always present; a value that does not apply is null rather than absent.

contract.description: Bumped only by a format change. An engine change that moves this number is a mistake in one direction; a format change that does not is a mistake in the other.

operation.description: Which call produced this. 'list': assignments in force at, above and below scope. 'assign': one assignment made or found. 'remove': one assignment removed or found already gone.

subscription.description: The subscription the scope is in. Source is 'scope' whenever the scope names one, which every scope but a management group does.

scope.description: The ARM id asked about, trailing slash removed but otherwise as given. For a remove, the scope the removed assignment was at.

assignee.description: The principal object id: the one a list was narrowed to, the one assigned, or the one the removed assignment was for. Null for an unnarrowed list and for a remove that found nothing.

outcome.description: What changed. Null for a list, which changes nothing. 'created': a new assignment was made. 'exists': an assignment giving the same role to the same principal at the same scope was already there -- under the name this tool derives, or under another (ARM's RoleAssignmentExists) -- and nothing was made. 'removed': the assignment was deleted. 'absent': there was no such assignment, which is the state a remove wanted.

principalNames.description: Can principalName be trusted to be filled in? 'resolved': every principal was found in the directory. 'partial': some were not (deleted principals keep their assignments). 'none': there were no principals to name. 'unavailable: <why>': the directory could not be read -- usually a guest account without directory read access -- so every principalName is null for that reason and not because the principal has no name.

assignments.description: Nearest first: assigned at the scope, then inherited from above it, then below it; within each, by scope then role. For an assign or a remove, the one assignment concerned; empty for 'absent'.

id.description: The assignment's full ARM id -- what azure_role_remove takes.

scope.description: Where the assignment is made, verbatim from ARM, whose casing of segments such as resourceGroups is not consistent.

relation.description: Where the assignment sits relative to the scope asked about, compared case-insensitively. 'at': at that scope. 'inherited': above it -- a parent resource group, the subscription, a management group or the root -- and so in force there. 'below': on something inside it, so in force there and not at the scope itself.

role.description: The role's name, e.g. Storage Blob Data Reader. Null when the role definition is not among the subscription's, such as one defined at a management group.

roleType.description: BuiltInRole or CustomRole. Null exactly when role is.

roleDefinitionId.description: The role definition's ARM id, verbatim.

principalType.description: User, Group, ServicePrincipal, ForeignGroup or whatever else ARM records. Null when ARM did not say.

principalName.description: A user's sign-in name, or a group's or service principal's display name. Null when the directory did not return the principal; principalNames says whether that is because it is gone or because the directory could not be asked.

description.description: The free-text description the assignment was made with. Null when it has none.

createdOn.description: When the assignment was made, verbatim from ARM. Null when ARM did not say.

createdBy.description: The object id of whoever made it, verbatim from ARM. Null when ARM did not say, as for assignments it made itself.

name.description: The subscription's display name when it was read from the Azure CLI profile. Null when it was taken from an id -- the caller's, or the scope's -- which is used as given without a lookup.

source.description: How it was decided. 'explicit': the caller named it, by id or by name. 'az default': the Azure CLI profile's default subscription. 'scope': read out of the ARM id the caller passed as a scope.
